## Simulation

Let's now discuss how we will simulate relative motion between the Chief and Deputy. Python has a library called SSAPy, which allows the user 
to model satellites in orbit using the two-body dynamics equation shown below.

$$
\ddot{\mathbf{r}} = -\frac{\mu}{r^3}\mathbf{r}
$${#eq-two_body}

By building some helper functions, we can allow two satellites to be propagated simultaneously for formation flight. This propagator will represent the 
truth model, and will be used for the Monte Carlo simulation discussed below. Another set of functions will be created to solve for the necessary State Transition Matrices in order to propagate 
the covariance forward in time, representing the linear covariance propagation. 

The Monte Carlo simulation will involve sampling N initial Deputy states (e.g. 500) from the distribution $\mathbf{x} \sim \mathcal{N}(\bar{\mathbf{x}}_0, \mathbf{P}_0)$ and then 
propagate them forward in time using the truth model for some number of orbits. $\mathbf{x}_0$ and $\mathbf{P}_0$ will then be propagated forward using @eq-lincov.
